clue.text: Punishment for French peer, royal cat's-paw

parts.note: a duc is a French duke, a peer of the realm
a king is a royal
a cat's-paw is a person used as a tool by another, a stooge or stool-pigeon, here a stool

explanation.surface: A French nobleman and a king's dupe face some penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-paw is someone made use of; STOOL (as in stool-pigeon) is the decoy or stooge sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair on which scolds and suspected witches were plunged into ponds was a historical penalty.

clue.text: How to get rid of Jack the Nipper

definitions.text: How to get rid of Jack the Nipper

parts.words: How to get rid of Jack the Nipper
parts.note: Jack Frost is the personification of nipping cold, so removing him means thawing out

explanation.surface: A recipe for disposing of a notorious villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack the Nipper' echoes Jack the Ripper, but means Jack Frost, who nips noses and fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Thawing out removes ice, the work of the folklore figure of hard weather.

clue.text: Giant policemen hold leaders of young Chelsea layabouts

indicators.note: hold means the police word grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: cops is slang for policemen

indicators.note: leaders of takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Police detain some young idlers from a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-eyed monster of Greek myth was a giant.

clue.text: But are scratch players so, easily annoyed ?

definitions.text: But are scratch players so, easily annoyed ?

parts.words: But are scratch players so, easily annoyed ?
parts.note: a scratch golfer with no handicap might be thought itchy, and the word for touchy also suggests something that can be made to itch

explanation.surface: Are top golfers quick to lose their temper?
explanation.walkthrough: A scratch player in golf has a handicap of zero; the clue plays on scratching an itch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being touchy and quick to anger is the plain sense, while skin that itches is the medical one.

clue.text: Hat to rock America !

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, Gib for short

explanation.surface: A hat to shake up America!
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like a verb but is Gibraltar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibus is a collapsible opera hat.

clue.text: A service in this, unusually dull

indicators.note: in sets the service inside the rearranged word
unusually signals the letters of this arranged in an odd way

parts.note: the Royal Navy is a service, RN

explanation.surface: A church service in this place is oddly lacklustre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the word this into TISH, and the service is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to dull or discolour a metal surface.

clue.text: Complex riddle-solver

definitions.meaning: Freud's complex named after the Theban king who wed his mother
the hero who answered the Sphinx's riddle

explanation.surface: Someone who cracks intricate puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud named a psychological complex after the Theban king, who also solved the Sphinx's riddle.

clue.text: A type of eagle, rook — or wool?

parts.note: the golden eagle is a species of eagle
to rook is to swindle, or fleece

explanation.surface: A bird of prey and a crow, or a ball of wool?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like the bird but is the verb meaning cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ram's coat sought by Jason and the Argonauts was golden wool.

clue.text: Man commanding about one hundred present

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for present is wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: to present is to offer
one is I, the Roman numeral
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A commander is present along with about a hundred others.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer is a person holding command in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Tedium, a sign of danger in time of prosperity

indicators.note: in tells us the sign of danger sits inside the time of prosperity

parts.note: a boom is a period of economic prosperity
red is the colour that signals danger

explanation.surface: Boredom sets in as a warning flag when times are good.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium and boredom are synonyms for weariness from dullness.

clue.text: Has first gardener turned up new sort of tater? That's crazy !

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the opening words are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Adam tended Eden, the first garden

indicators.note: new sort of signals the letters rearranged into a fresh form

explanation.surface: Has the first gardener dug up an odd potato variety? Madness!
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' runs HAS and ADAM backwards together as MADASAH; 'new sort of' rearranges TATER into ATTER. Hatters were proverbially mad from mercury poisoning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares madness to Victorian hat-makers poisoned by mercury.

clue.text: Parachutist found "underneath the arches" ?

definitions.meaning: someone who drops out of an aircraft
a vagrant who has quit society and sleeps rough under railway arches, as in the old music-hall song

explanation.surface: Where would a parachutist end up but sleeping under the arches?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underneath the Arches' is a famous British music-hall song about tramps sleeping rough beneath railway arches.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-out leaves conventional society, and literally one drops out of a plane with a chute.

clue.text: Unleashed one sort of disc

definitions.meaning: let off the leash, as a dog ... its collar
a ... disc is a displaced spinal disc

explanation.surface: A dog let off its lead and a back injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip a hound is to release it from the leash; a slipped disc is a common spinal injury.

clue.text: Money in bars ?

definitions.meaning: musical ... are written within bars of music

explanation.surface: Is money kept in gold bars?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests gold bullion, but these are the bars of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper currency is banknotes, and musical sounds written on a stave fill the bars.

clue.text: Billy chewed over this point with men of religion

parts.note: Billy Budd is the title sailor of Melville's novel

indicators.note: chewed over suggests the letters of this being mangled into a new order

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A boy called Billy ponders this matter with clergymen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed over' shuffles THIS into HIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the Buddha form a religious community, monks among them.

clue.text: Eccentric VIP's a lord-this shows it's wrong

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so these letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: the letters of VIP with its S, as printed

explanation.surface: An odd bigwig, a peer, proves a point wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A disproof, showing something false, is a refutation.

clue.text: Feathery feature of the dawn sky

definitions.text: Feathery feature of the dawn sky

parts.words: Feathery feature of the dawn sky
parts.note: a quality of being feather-weight, and also the paleness that spreads over the sky at daybreak

explanation.surface: Wispy clouds catch the eye at sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of weighing little like a feather, and the brightening of a morning sky, share one word.

clue.text: Variety of Tangier rock

indicators.note: variety of means a different arrangement of the city's letters

explanation.surface: A kind of stone from Morocco's port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangier rock' suggests a geological sample from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous stone.

clue.text: Wine in the latter end proves more toothsome

indicators.note: in puts the wine inside the closing letters
end takes the closing letters of the word latter

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Wine in the end proves more delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means tasty, so more toothsome is more delicious.

clue.text: Fishes caught by Tom, going to church

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A tomcat snatches fish before going off to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name, but it is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish taken by an angler on a trip are the day's haul.

clue.text: Littlefellow's wreath ?

parts.note: a garland whose name reads as a man with a diminutive ending attached, a small fellow

explanation.surface: A small man wears a garland.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as CHAP (fellow) with -LET (little, as in piglet), the word for a wreath.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland worn on the head.

clue.text: Odd promotion, Old Rugbeian leaving to become watchman !

indicators.note: odd signals the letters strangely ordered

parts.note: OR is the abbreviation for Old Rugbeian, a former pupil of Rugby School

explanation.surface: An odd promotion as a former schoolboy becomes a night watchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is an English public school; take O and R out of PROMOTION, 'leaving', and rearrange. Thomas Tompion was a famous clock- and watchmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tompion was the celebrated seventeenth-century English clock and watch maker.

clue.text: Passes as 22's amendment

indicators.note: an amendment alters the letters into a new order

parts.note: 22 refers to the answer to 22 down, slumber

explanation.surface: A motion passes as an amendment to clause 22.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amendment' rearranges AS with SLEEP, the answer to 22 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that passes is said to elapse.

clue.text: John's up, roused from this ?

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: John Peel, the huntsman of the song, possessive Peel's

explanation.surface: John has got up after being woken.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel is the huntsman of the folk song 'D'ye ken John Peel'.
explanation.definitionFit: One is roused from slumber.

clue.text: Let in again, having to send about a penny (old money)

indicators.note: about places the sending word around the other letters

parts.note: to remit is to send money
D was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British coinage

explanation.surface: Readmitted after sending a penny in pre-decimal coin.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain's pre-1971 money a penny was written d, from the Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: To readmit is to allow back in after an absence.

clue.text: Note the bones, if entering this building

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: entering puts the little word inside the bones

parts.note: bones is slang for dice

explanation.surface: Note the skeleton, if you go into this building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bones' is an old slang name for dice.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure.

clue.text: Foxy Arsene confounded in day of victory

indicators.note: in places the shuffled thief inside the day of victory

parts.note: VE Day was Victory in Europe day, 8 May 1945

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, rearranging the thief's surname

parts.note: Arsene Lupin is the gentleman thief of Maurice Leblanc's stories

explanation.surface: A cunning football manager is muddled on the day of a win.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsene is not the football manager here but the fictional French thief; 'confounded' mixes his surname into ULPIN. VE Day is the 1945 Allied victory in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulpine means of or like a fox, and so cunning.

clue.text: London's archiepiscopal line?

parts.note: one of London's Underground lines shares its name with an archbishop presiding over a province

explanation.surface: Is there a line of archbishops in London?
explanation.walkthrough: The Metropolitan is a London Underground line; a metropolitan is also a senior archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A presiding archbishop of a province bears the same title as one of London's Tube lines.
